Neither solution is correct. The correct answer is **42 inches**.

Each equilateral triangle has perimeter 21, so its side length is 7. In a regular hexagon divided into six equilateral triangles from the center, each triangle's side is also a side of the hexagon. So the hexagon has six sides of length 7, giving a perimeter of 6 × 7 = 42.

**Solution A (126)** wrongly assumes each triangle's side is one-sixth of the hexagon's perimeter (P_t = P_h / 6). That relation is false. Its later steps are internally consistent, but the starting relation is wrong, so the result is 3 times too large.

**Solution B (36)** also rests on a false premise, the proportion 21/3 = x/6, which would imply each triangle's side is one-sixth of the perimeter. Its arithmetic is also off: 21/3 = 7 and 7 = x/6 gives x = 42, not 36. It contains a second error on top of the flawed setup.

Both answers are wrong. Solution B is closer to the correct value (36 versus 42), so I select it as the marginally less incorrect of the two, but neither has a meaningful chance of being right.

WINNER: B
